text: Communication is constantly underrated. And communication isn't about being able to convey a message, it's about being able to convey a message in a way that the listener receives it, and understands it, and remembers it. And that's really hard to do.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Gina begins the podcast by sharing one of her key beliefs about effective communication. She's discussing how true communication goes far beyond simply delivering information - it requires ensuring the message is not only heard but actually absorbed and retained by the audience. This insight reflects her experience in growth marketing and brand building at companies like Duolingo.
text_ko: 커뮤니케이션(communication)은 늘 과소평가돼요. 단순히 메시지를 전달할 수 있다는 게 중요한 게 아니라, 듣는 사람이 그걸 받아들이고 이해하고 기억하게끔 전달하는 방식이 진짜 중요한 거예요. 그걸 해내기는 정말 어려워요.
text_zh: 大家总是小看沟通的重要性。沟通不是说你能把话说出来就行了，关键是你得让听的人能接收到、听明白、还能记住，这才是真正的沟通。这个真的很难做到。
text_es: La comunicación siempre está súper subestimada. Y comunicar no se trata de poder transmitir un mensaje, sino de poder transmitirlo de tal manera que quien te escucha lo reciba, lo entienda y se acuerde de él. Y eso es realmente difícil de lograr.
key_sentence: Communication is constantly underrated; conveying a message is really hard to do.

vocabulary.definition: To communicate or express an idea, feeling, or piece of information to someone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, conveying a message effectively is crucial for ensuring that stakeholders understand the objectives and goals of a project or initiative.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'convey' implies the transfer of information, it often carries the connotation of doing so in a clear and impactful manner.

vocabulary.definition: The act of exchanging information, ideas, or feelings between individuals or groups through speaking, writing, or other mediums.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective communication is foundational in business environments, facilitating collaboration, negotiation, and relationship-building among teams and clients.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'communication' encompasses both verbal and non-verbal forms, and its effectiveness can vary based on context and audience.

text: One of the things I've helped employ at Duolingo that I think is still there today, it's definitely not just me, it was an amazing team, is a unique voice.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks about what made Duolingo successful as one of the rare consumer subscription apps that thrived. Gina explains how Duolingo differentiated itself from typical educational apps by developing a distinctive brand voice that was quirky, funny, and emotionally engaging rather than just instructional. She emphasizes that creating an emotional connection with users was crucial to the app's growth and retention.
text_ko: 제가 듀오링고에서 도입하는 데 기여했고 지금도 남아 있다고 생각하는 것 중 하나는 바로 특유의 목소리예요. 물론 저 혼자 한 건 아니고, 정말 멋진 팀이 있었어요.
text_zh: 我在多邻国帮着打造的一个东西，现在应该还在用，当然不是我一个人的功劳，是整个团队都很棒，就是打造了一个很独特的品牌声音。
text_es: Una de las cosas que ayudé a desarrollar en Duolingo y que creo que sigue ahí hoy en día, aunque definitivamente no fue solo yo sino un equipo increíble, es una voz única.
original_text: One of the things I've helped employ at Duolingo that I think is still there today, it's definitely not just me, it was an amazing team, is a unique voice. And what that means is not just another language learning app where we give you instructions and you follow directions. There is always a quirk, like it's unexpected. The way we talk to you is a little bit funny. It doesn't take ourselves too seriously and it makes the person receiving this message feel something.

vocabulary.definition: Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.
vocabulary.businessContext: A unique selling proposition (USP) is vital for businesses to attract customers by offering something that competitors do not.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'unique' suggests exclusivity, it can sometimes be overused in marketing, leading to skepticism if not substantiated.

vocabulary.definition: To make use of or apply a particular method, tool, or resource for a specific purpose.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, to employ a strategy or technology means to integrate it into operations to achieve desired outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a formal connotation, suggesting a deliberate and strategic application rather than casual use.

text: We are very encouraged in our lives, especially professionally, to talk about our A-sides all the time. Because that's what impresses people, that's what opens doors, that's what allows us to keep growing and it's so important.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks Gina to explain her concept of A-side and B-side, which she referenced from her conference talk. Gina uses the analogy of vinyl records having an A-side (the hit song) and B-side (the lesser-known track) to describe how people only share their successes publicly while hiding their struggles and failures. She argues that this creates an unrealistic 'Instagram-perfect' narrative that doesn't reflect the full reality of anyone's journey.
text_ko: 특히 직장에서는 우리에게 항상 자기의 A-사이드(A-sides)만 얘기하라고 많이 권장해요. 사람들이 인상을 받게 하는 것도 그거고, 기회를 열어주는 것도 그거고, 계속 성장할 수 있게 해주는 것도 바로 그거라서요. 그래서 정말 중요해요.
text_zh: 不管是生活中还是工作中，大家都特别鼓励我们要多展示自己的优点和强项。因为这样才能给别人留下好印象，才能为自己打开机会的大门，才能让我们不断成长进步，这确实很重要。
text_es: Nos animan mucho en la vida, sobre todo en el trabajo, a hablar siempre de nuestros puntos fuertes. Porque eso es lo que impresiona a la gente, lo que abre puertas, lo que nos permite seguir creciendo y es súper importante.
key_sentence: Because that's what impresses people, that's what opens doors, that's what allows us to keep growing and it's so important.
original_text: We are very encouraged in our lives, especially professionally, to talk about our A-sides all the time. Because that's what impresses people, that's what opens doors, that's what allows us to keep growing and it's so important. It means that a lot of what you hear in podcasts and on stage ends up being the Instagramable version of someone, or a company, or a country's trajectory. It's just the highlights.

vocabulary.definition: To be given support, confidence, or hope to do something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being encouraged often refers to receiving positive feedback or motivation from colleagues or leaders, which can enhance performance and morale.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'encouraged' generally has a positive connotation, it may imply a need for external validation rather than intrinsic motivation.

vocabulary.definition: To make someone feel admiration or respect for something or someone.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the corporate world, impressing clients or stakeholders is crucial for building relationships and securing deals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a superficial admiration; thus, it is important to ensure that what impresses is also substantive and genuine.

vocabulary.definition: To create opportunities or possibilities for advancement or success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, networking and showcasing achievements can open doors to new partnerships, promotions, or market opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive approach to career development, but it can also imply that opportunities may be contingent on external factors.

vocabulary.definition: Increasing in size, number, or importance over time.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, growing often refers to the expansion of a company’s market share, revenue, or workforce, indicating overall success and sustainability.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'growing' is generally positive, it can also imply challenges related to scalability and resource management.

text: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks Gina to share a B-side story from her life. Gina recounts her early struggles, including dropping out of college due to depression, having a college counselor tell her she had 'nothing to show for' her time, and facing multiple job rejections and layoffs. From these experiences, she learned an important lesson about the psychology of career advancement and how perception matters as much as actual accomplishments.
text_ko: 제가 거기서 얻은 한 가지 깨달음이 있어요. 지금까지도 남아 있고 다른 사람들에게도 도움이 될 것 같아요. 실제로 의미 있는 일을 하고 배우는 것만으로는 충분하지 않더라고요.
text_zh: 我在那里学到的一个道理，到现在还记得很清楚，我觉得对别人也有用，就是不能光做那些真正重要的事情，光学习还不够。
text_es: Lo que más me quedó de esa experiencia, y creo que le puede servir a otros también, es que no se trata solo de hacer cosas que realmente importan y de aprender.
key_sentence: it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning.
original_text: My one learning there that has stuck with me, and I think can work for other people too, is that it's not just about doing things that actually matter, and learning. It's about being able to tell the story, and it's about understanding what other people perceive as valuable.

vocabulary.definition: The process of acquiring knowledge, skills, or competencies through experience, study, or instruction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, learning is crucial for employee development, innovation, and adapting to changing market conditions.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with formal education, 'learning' can also refer to informal or experiential knowledge gained in the workplace.

vocabulary.definition: To have significance or importance in a particular context or situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, focusing on what 'actually matters' helps prioritize tasks and initiatives that drive value and impact for the organization.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes the distinction between superficial tasks and those that contribute meaningfully to goals or outcomes.

text: So we deployed historic amounts of money in the campaign. It wasn't me, Gina, personally. I think that's important to share. So my Bloomberg presidential campaign was spending roughly a million dollars a day. Which is crazy.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks Gina about her experience working on Mike Bloomberg's presidential campaign, specifically about deploying a historic amount of money on paid advertising. Gina clarifies that while the campaign as a whole spent massive amounts (around $1 million per day), she personally wasn't responsible for that entire budget. She's setting up to share lessons learned from working with such unprecedented advertising spend.
text_ko: 그래서 캠페인에 역대급 규모의 자금을 투입했어요. 그건 저나 지나 개인이 부담한 건 아니에요. 이 점은 꼭 공유해야 한다고 생각해요. 제 블룸버그 대선 캠페인은 하루에 대략 백만 달러씩 쓰고 있었어요. 정말 말도 안 되는 수준이에요.
text_zh: 所以我们在竞选活动中投入了史无前例的资金。这不是我吉娜个人的钱，我觉得这点很重要要说清楚。我们彭博总统竞选团队当时每天烧钱大概一百万美元。这简直太疯狂了。
text_es: Entonces desplegamos cantidades históricas de dinero en la campaña. No fui yo, Gina, personalmente. Me parece importante aclarar eso. La campaña presidencial de Bloomberg estaba gastando aproximadamente un millón de dólares al día. Lo cual es una locura.
key_sentence: We deployed historic amounts of money, spending roughly a million dollars a day.
original_text: So we deployed historic amounts of money in the campaign. It wasn't me, Gina, personally. I think that's important to share. So my Bloomberg presidential campaign was spending roughly a million dollars a day. Which is crazy. And you can do a lot with a million dollars a day.

vocabulary.definition: To deploy means to strategically position or utilize resources, personnel, or technology for a specific purpose or mission.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'deployed' often refers to the allocation of financial resources, human capital, or technology in order to achieve operational goals or execute strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'deployed' conveys a sense of intentionality and strategic planning, it may not be appropriate in casual contexts where simpler terms like 'used' might suffice.

vocabulary.definition: Historic refers to something that is significant in history or has lasting importance, often relating to events, decisions, or achievements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'historic' can describe milestones, financial achievements, or strategic decisions that have a profound impact on the company's trajectory or industry.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'historic' carries a weight of importance and should be used when referring to events that will be remembered or studied in the future, rather than trivial occurrences.

vocabulary.definition: A campaign is a coordinated series of activities or efforts aimed at achieving a specific goal, often in marketing, political, or social contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a campaign typically refers to marketing initiatives designed to promote products, services, or brand awareness, often involving multiple channels and strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'campaign' implies a planned and organized effort, and should be used when discussing initiatives that are strategic rather than ad hoc or spontaneous.

vocabulary.definition: Spending refers to the act of using financial resources to purchase goods, services, or investments, often measured over a specific period.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, 'spending' is closely monitored as it affects budgeting, financial forecasting, and overall profitability, with a focus on return on investment.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'spending' is a neutral term, it can carry negative connotations if associated with wastefulness or excessive costs, so it's important to contextualize it appropriately.

text: Which is, once you click on an ad, you land somewhere. And then whatever happens there is super important. Because if people then take the action you want them to take on that landing page, or don't, is definitive.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Gina is explaining what she learned from working on the Bloomberg campaign with their massive advertising budget. She describes how there were many talented people focused on creating and optimizing ads, but she realized that most people overlook what happens after someone clicks an ad - the landing page experience. She decided to focus her efforts on optimizing landing pages rather than competing with others on ad creation, which proved highly effective.
text_ko: 광고(ad)를 클릭하면 특정 랜딩 페이지(landing page)로 연결되잖아요. 그곳에서 무슨 일이 벌어지는지가 정말 중요해요. 사람들이 그 랜딩 페이지에서 우리가 원하는 행동을 하느냐 안 하느냐가 결국 모든 걸 결정해요.
text_zh: 就是说，用户点击广告之后，会跳转到一个页面。接下来在那个页面上发生的事情就特别关键了。因为用户在那个落地页(landing page)上到底会不会按你希望的去操作，基本上就能决定成败了。
text_es: O sea, una vez que haces clic en un anuncio, llegas a algún lado. Y lo que pase ahí es súper importante. Porque si la gente hace lo que tú quieres que haga en esa página de destino (landing page), o no lo hace, eso ya es definitivo.
key_sentence: whatever happens there is super important.
original_text: Which is, once you click on an ad, you land somewhere. And then whatever happens there is super important. Because if people then take the action you want them to take on that landing page, or don't, is definitive. But everyone spends all of their effort and money on the ads.

vocabulary.definition: Serving to provide a final solution or conclusion; decisive.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a definitive decision or document is one that is conclusive and leaves no room for doubt, often used in contracts or strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'definitive' implies certainty, it can also suggest a lack of flexibility, so it should be used when emphasizing finality.

vocabulary.definition: A standalone web page created specifically for a marketing or advertising campaign, designed to direct visitors to take a specific action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In digital marketing, a landing page is crucial for converting visitors into leads or customers by focusing on a single call to action.
vocabulary.nuance: The effectiveness of a landing page can vary based on design and content, so it should be tailored to the target audience and campaign goals.

text: Very few people really believed that we were going to make it, not surprisingly. Even though we had this amazing team, et cetera, now it looks almost obvious, it's like B to C language learning just seems so niche.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks Gina what Duolingo did right to become one of the rare successful consumer subscription businesses, noting that most B2C subscription apps fail. Gina explains that initially, few people believed Duolingo would succeed because language learning seemed like a niche market and education technology was seen as unprofitable. She's setting up to explain what factors actually made Duolingo successful despite these perceived limitations.
text_ko: 우리가 성공할 거라고 진짜로 믿은 사람은 거의 없었어요. 놀랍지 않아요. 훌륭한 팀도 있었고 여러 조건이 맞았는데도, 지금 보면 거의 당연해 보이죠. 소비자 대상(B2C) 언어 학습은 그냥 너무 틈새 시장처럼 보였으니까요.
text_zh: 说实话，当时几乎没人相信我们能成功，这也不奇怪。虽然我们团队很厉害什么的，现在回头看好像很明显，但当时B to C的语言学习看起来就是个很小众的市场。
text_es: Muy poca gente realmente creía que íbamos a lograrlo, y no es sorpresa. Aunque teníamos este equipo increíble y todo eso, ahora parece casi obvio, es como que el aprendizaje de idiomas B2C (business to consumer) se veía súper de nicho.
key_sentence: Very few believed we would make it; education seems so niche with no money.
original_text: Very few people really believed that we were going to make it, not surprisingly. Even though we had this amazing team, et cetera, now it looks almost obvious, it's like B to C language learning just seems so niche. And plus education, there's no money in education. It's been stuck for so long.

vocabulary.definition: A niche refers to a specialized segment of the market for a particular kind of product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying a niche allows companies to target specific customer needs and differentiate themselves from competitors, often leading to higher customer loyalty.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'niche' can suggest a limited market, it often connotes a unique opportunity for businesses to excel in less saturated areas.

vocabulary.definition: Believed is the past tense of 'believe,' meaning to accept something as true or to have confidence in the existence or reliability of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, the term often reflects the confidence stakeholders have in a project's success or the validity of a business idea, influencing investment and strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a degree of skepticism or doubt, especially when used in contexts where success was uncertain.

vocabulary.definition: An amazing team refers to a group of individuals who work exceptionally well together, often characterized by high levels of collaboration, skill, and motivation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and businesses, having an amazing team is often cited as a critical factor for success, as it fosters innovation and effective problem-solving.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase conveys strong positive connotations, suggesting not just competence but also enthusiasm and synergy among team members.
